page.title: Hedging and Cautious Language Basics
page.subtitle_html: Hedging and Cautious Language Basics - B2 cautious language for claims, opinions, and academic-style statements.
page.subtitle_text: B2 cautious language for claims, opinions, and academic-style statements.

blocks.body: {"level":"B2","intro":"Hedging and Cautious Language Basics: compact B2 anchors for making statements less absolute and more careful.","rules":[{"label":"Cautious verbs","text":"Use seem, appear, tend to, and suggest to soften claims.","example":"The results seem to support the idea."},{"label":"Cautious adverbs","text":"Use probably, possibly, generally, or relatively when the claim is not absolute.","example":"This approach is generally more effective."},{"label":"Careful conclusions","text":"Use may, might, and could to express possible conclusions.","example":"This change may reduce the risk."}]}

blocks.heading: B2 focus
blocks.body: This compact page exists as the theory anchor for the English Sentence Builder B2 lesson package.

page.title: Hedging and Cautious Language
page.subtitle_html: Hedging and Cautious Language - C1 cautious claims, probability, limited evidence, and academic register.
page.subtitle_text: C1 cautious claims, probability, limited evidence, and academic register.

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Hedging and Cautious Language: C1 anchors for making claims precise, cautious, and academically appropriate.","rules":[{"label":"Cautious verbs","text":"Use seem, appear, suggest, indicate, or tend to when evidence is not absolute.","example":"The findings seem to support this view."},{"label":"Modals of possibility","text":"Use may, might, could, and would appear to avoid overstatement.","example":"This may be related to the wider context."},{"label":"Limits and concessions","text":"Acknowledge limits with to some extent, not necessarily, or it should be acknowledged that.","example":"It should be acknowledged that the evidence remains limited."}]}

blocks.heading: C1 focus
blocks.body: This compact page exists as the theory anchor for the English Sentence Builder C1 hedging and cautious language lesson package.

page.title: Stance Register And Evaluation
page.subtitle_html: Stance Register And Evaluation - C2 cautious claims, evaluative language, and precise academic register.
page.subtitle_text: C2 cautious claims, evaluative language, and precise academic register.

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"Stance, register and evaluation: compact C2 anchors for positioning claims without sounding over-certain or informal.","rules":[{"label":"Hedged stance","text":"Use it could be argued that, it is possible that, and appears to when evidence needs careful framing.","example":"It could be argued that the results remain inconclusive."},{"label":"Evaluative precision","text":"Choose evaluative adjectives and nouns that match the strength of the evidence.","example":"The proposal represents a significant but limited improvement."},{"label":"Register control","text":"Prefer formal, balanced phrasing in academic or professional contexts.","example":"The evidence suggests a cautious interpretation of the trend."}]}

blocks.heading: C2 focus
blocks.body: This compact page anchors the English Sentence Builder C2 lesson on stance, register and evaluation.
